tob-10784: C. J. S. Thompson’s richly illustrated history traces alchemy from ancient Egypt through the medieval adepts to the birth of modern chemistry and pharmacy. He tells of the search for the philosopher’s stone and the elixir of life, along with the quacks and visionaries who pursued them. The book captures the romance of a science that was half magic and half experiment.
tob-4184: Diogenes Laertius is our tale-bearer of Greek thought — his Lives keep the quips, habits, and teachings of all, from Thales to Epicurus. Without him we would know far less of the old sages. C. D. Yonge’s rendering brings this needful, ever-amusing storehouse to English readers.
tob-4284: Budge’s Book of the Dead musters the Egyptian charms for threading the underworld — the pleas before the two-and-forty judges, the words of power, the charts of the night. His rendering, long the standard, made the papyri speak plain. The book is old Egypt’s handbook for forever.
tob-4161-70484: The second volume of Tylor’s Primitive Culture turns to tale, rite, and wonder-working — showing how rites and stories spell early man’s reading of the world. His matching way set the mold for man-lore. The two books together stay the field’s founding text.
tob-0184: G. R. S. Mead’s book gives the Hymn of the Pearl — the Gnostic song of a prince who sinks into Egypt to win a pearl, forgetting then minded of his kingly birth. Few soul-parables sing so fair. Mead’s Englishing and gloss light its deeps.
tob-14184: R. H. Charles’s Old Testament Cast-Out Books muster the uncanon’d books in clear English. His learned Englishings, with notes and fore-words, made these olden texts open to all. Scholars still start here. The gathering stays the standard English handbook for the field.
cia-0000118684: A January 1971 document, estimated date, on a new mobilization group meeting the press in Hanoi — the archive's spelling says mobilizaitn. North Vietnam was rallying its population for the long war's next phase. The entry shows the CIA reading Hanoi's domestic propaganda for signs of strain or resolve.
cia-0000119584: A November 1963 report on political crisis in Czechoslovakia. Five years before Soviet tanks crushed the Prague Spring, the party was already in turmoil. The document shows the CIA spotting trouble early in a satellite state — though no one foresaw how it would end.
cia-0000126884: An October 1968 report on the Czechoslovak leadership facing an uncertain future. The reformers were still in office but living on borrowed time — Moscow's patience was finite. The document captures the slow strangulation of the Prague Spring, month by month.
cia-0000132284: Situation Report 593 with a special spot commentary: Saddam calling for something — the truncated title cuts off the appeal. Spot commentaries flagged moments too urgent for the routine format. The document is the dictator's voice, amplified and analyzed.
cia-0000132484: Item three in the April 1960 series: American refineries in Cuba ordered to process Soviet crude oil. Havana's order was a provocation — and a trap. The document captures the moment the oil war began: the refineries, the crude, and the coming seizures.
cia-0000132684: A 1961 Latin America item: the Cuban situation. The companion to its twin, one entry apart. The document is the update: the situation, restated.
cia-0000135884: A 1954 pouch manifest from LINCOLN. The diplomatic pouch carried the operation's paper — manifests listed what went in. The entry is the inventory: the pouch, itemized.
cia-0000135984: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN reporting Calligeris's contact with Panama's President Remon — the truncated title cuts off the details. The exile leader was courting the region's strongmen. The document is the courtship: the contact, made.
un-ga-res-384: Resolution 384 of the General Assembly, adopted in 1950. The Korean War year's Assembly. The catalog keeps the number and year; the resolution keeps its judgment.
un-ga-res-a-69-84: Resolution A/69/84, cataloged with the year 2013 — a year before the session, a small inconsistency. The designation is kept; the date is noted with doubt.
un-sc-res-84: Security Council Resolution 84, adopted in July 1950 — the resolution that placed the defense of South Korea under a unified United Nations command led by the United States. With the Soviet Union boycotting the Council, the West turned the Korean War into the UN's war. The resolution is the command: the flag, united.
un-sc-res-284: Security Council Resolution 284, adopted in 1970. The Council deliberated. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-384: Security Council Resolution 384, adopted in December 1975 — the East Timor resolution, deploring Indonesia's invasion and demanding withdrawal. Days after the invasion, the Council spoke for the occupied territory. The resolution is the condemnation: the invasion, deplored.
un-sc-res-884: Security Council Resolution 884, adopted in 1993 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-984: Security Council Resolution 984, adopted in 1995 — aligned. The Council deciding. The designation and year are preserved; the act belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-1284: Security Council Resolution 1284, cataloged with the year 1995 — though the famous Iraq inspections resolution of that number belongs to 1999, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned — and the subject is left to the text.
un-sc-res-1684: Security Council Resolution 1684, cataloged with the year 2008 — the historical record places this Yugoslavia tribunal judges resolution in June 2006. The designation is kept; the catalog's date is questioned.
cia-0000132784: A 1960 CIA Cuban developments file — number 0000132784. The series rolls on. The entry is the roll: the developments, filed.
cia-0000136784: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136784. The fateful year's archive. The document is the archive: the year, 1961.
cia-0000138984: A 1946 CIA military information file on Russian aid to Chinese communists, numbered 0000138984. The postwar watch on the Sino-Soviet link. The document is the aid: the alliance, forming.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d84: Generalissimo Chiang to President Roosevelt, November 2, 1943 — Document 84. November opened with China's answer. The message is the answer: Chiang, replying.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d184: The Secretary of State to the President, November 2, 1943 — Document 184. A second that day. The memo is the doubling: the day, busy.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d284: A note by the secretaries of the Joint Chiefs of Staff — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 284. The staff's note. The note is the staff's: the secretaries, noting.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d384: Foreign Commissar Molotov to President Roosevelt — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 384. Moscow's foreign minister wrote the president directly. The note is the minister's: Molotov, to Roosevelt.
arxiv-2605-08784: Online stores need endless product posters, and AI-generated advertising art is becoming the cheap way to make them. Benlei Cui and eight coauthors offer SIMPLEPOSTER, a deliberately plain baseline for automatic poster generation. The point of the 2026 paper is honesty in comparison: by showing what a no-frills method achieves, it gives every fancier approach something solid to beat.
arxiv-2605-08884: Ricci shrinkers are special shapes that evolve under Ricci flow by simply shrinking — they model how singularities form in geometry. Pak-Yeung Chan and Yongjia Zhang prove rigidity and gap theorems for them, showing these shapes are far more constrained than they look. The 2026 paper is pure differential geometry on the anatomy of singularities.
arxiv-2605-08984: FPGAs reconfigure themselves from bitstreams, and a malicious one can hijack the hardware. Rye Stahle-Smith, Carter Antley, Jason D. Bakos, and colleagues screen bitstreams at line rate — as fast as they arrive — using hardware acceleration. The 2026 paper is hardware security: inspecting the goods before the gates open.
arxiv-2605-09184: Ontologies — formal maps of what exists in a domain — are painful to build and merge by hand. Fabio Rovai proposes open ontologies: tool-augmented engineering with stable matching alignment to reconcile competing maps. The 2026 paper is knowledge representation with algorithmic diplomacy.
arxiv-2605-09284: Mesh-based simulations — weather, airflow — are accurate only on fine meshes, which cost dearly. Jiyeon Kim, Youngjoon Hong, and Won-Yong Shin bring neural super-resolution to the rescue, sharpening coarse simulations with semi-supervised learning. The 2026 paper gets fine-mesh accuracy on a coarse-mesh budget.
arxiv-2605-09384: Doctors asking questions about medical images need AI that reasons step by step — chain of thought — without retraining giants. Runze Ma, Shunbo Jia, Haonan Lyu, and colleagues adapt efficiently with LiteMedCoT-VL. The 2026 paper is medical visual question answering on a budget.
arxiv-2605-09584: Hospital inpatients need decisions supported by open-ended reasoning, not multiple choice. Aishik Nagar, Arun-Kumar Kaliya-Perumal, Yu-Hsuan Han, and colleagues reinforce that reasoning with outcome-aware rubrics — CLR-voyance. The 2026 paper is clinical AI for the ward.
arxiv-2605-09684: AI agents need monitors watching them, and those monitors themselves need red-teaming. Monika Jotautaitė, Maria Angelica Martinez, Ollie Matthews, and colleagues build MonitoringBench: semi-automated red-teaming for agent monitoring. The 2026 paper tests the watchers before the watched misbehave.
arxiv-2605-09884: The moon's cratering is asymmetric — one face bears more scars — and lunar ejecta may be the missing piece resolving the puzzle. Hailiang Li, Xiaoping Zhang, and Li-Yong Zhou make the case. The 2026 paper is planetary science on the moon's lopsided history.
arxiv-2605-09984: 4D generation — three dimensions plus time — needs grounding in physical reality; geometric 4D stitching provides it. Sunwoo Park, Taesung Kwon, and Jong Chul Ye develop the stitching method. The 2026 paper is generative 4D, stitched to the ground. It grounds generated worlds in geometry.
arxiv-2605-10084: Audio representations disentangled by power for generative modeling — PoDAR separates loudness from content. Alejandro Luebs, Mithilesh Vaidya, Ishaan Kumar, and colleagues build it. The 2026 paper is audio generation with disentangled power. It cleanly separates power from sound.
plos-pone-0003384: Cell biologists probed a gene-silencing protein's quieter role in this 2008 paper. MBP-1 was known as a general repressor whose overabundance kills cancer cells, but the team did the reverse: dialing it down in normal human skin fibroblasts. The cells aged prematurely through the p53-p21 pathway, showing that natural MBP-1 levels normally hold cellular aging in check.
plos-pone-0003484: Behavioral ecologists documented deadly romance paying off in this 2008 field study. In a wild population where females frequently eat their mates, the team measured the costs to males against the nutritional benefits to females. Sexual cannibalism emerged not as a glitch but as a strategy, with females gaining real reproductive advantages from devouring suitors.
plos-pone-0003584: Botanists proved museum drawers hold readable DNA in this 2008 methods paper. From just 2 milligrams of herbarium specimens up to 129 years old, the team amplified a 620-base stretch of the cox2 gene, comparing 19 extraction methods. The success turns dried plant collections into a time machine for evolutionary and biodiversity studies.
plos-pone-0003684: In 2008, Tricco, Brehaut, and Chen audited the Cochrane review pipeline. Tracking 411 published protocols to completion, they asked which ones actually became finished reviews and why others stalled. The retrospective look measures the gap between starting a gold-standard review and finishing one.
plos-pone-0003784: Halpern, Ogunsola, and Obunge tested a vaginal gel against HIV in this 2008 trial. The phase II study measured whether 6 percent cellulose sulfate gel could block male-to-female HIV transmission. The trial put a much-hoped prevention tool to a rigorous test.
plos-pone-0003884: In 2008, Kent and Meredith found potassium channels keeping the brain's clock ticking. BK channels regulated the rhythmic firing of neurons in the suprachiasmatic nucleus, the body's master pacemaker. The result ties daily rhythms to the electrical beat of clock cells.
plos-pone-0003984: In 2008, Ben-Simon, Podlipsky, and Arieli found the resting brain double-booked. Two distinct alpha-rhythm processes ran at once in the supposedly idle brain. The alpha rhythm, long called the idle signature, turned out to multitask. The result complicates the very idea of a brain ever truly at rest.
plos-pone-0004084: In 2008, a Spanish team tested handouts for a dying vulture. Supplementary feeding aimed to lift the endangered vulture's odds. The team weighed the practice's power to boost population viability. Feeding stations emerged as a practical lifeline for the hungry birds.
plos-pone-0004184: In 2009, a Japanese team found mouse embryos stalling without a copier. DNA polymerase delta proved vital for early mammal embryo growth. Losing the copy enzyme halted growth at the start. The finding pins a core copier to life's very start.
plos-pone-0004284: In 2009, a team found a tag-adding enzyme tuning tiny worm synapses. RPM-1 and the p38 MAPK PMK-3 steered AMPA receptor delivery jointly. The worm's nerve junctions needed the enzyme's order badly. The route links tagging to learning gear quite directly.
plos-pone-0350884: Hydrogen can store energy for entire neighborhoods, but running a hydrogen-powered microgrid means juggling power flows and carbon costs at the same time. This paper presents a distributed optimization method that manages electricity and carbon together across a microgrid with hydrogen storage. The approach aims at cleaner, cheaper local power that adapts as prices and demand shift.
plos-pone-0357284: Run-off-road crashes kill on rural highways — and the roadside design decides how often. This paper developed evidence-based clear-zone design for mitigating run-off-road and rollover crashes on Saudi Arabia’s rural highways. The design rules give engineers proven ways to make roadsides forgiving when drivers err.
plos-pone-0357584: Melatonin does more than govern sleep — its gene network may predict cancer outcomes. This paper found prognostic value in melatonin-related signature genes in lung adenocarcinoma. The gene signature could help oncologists forecast which patients face the toughest course and treat them accordingly.
plos-pone-0358184: Carbon-ion therapy demands precise stopping-power maps to hit tumors and spare healthy tissue. This paper measured the impact of dual-layer spectral CT-derived stopping power ratios on single-energy CT-based carbon-ion treatment planning for thoracic cancer. The comparison sharpens targeting for hard-to-treat chest tumors.
plos-pone-0357784: The sharing economy promises opportunity for all — but the reality is uneven. This qualitative text analysis from focus groups explored digital inequalities in the sharing economy. The participants’ voices reveal who gets locked out of the platform promise and which barriers keep them out.
plos-pone-0357984: Dialysis patients accumulate indoxyl sulfate — a gut-derived toxin that inflames blood vessels. This paper showed vitamin D alleviates its inflammatory and cholesterol-disrupting effects in macrophages, with direct implications for vascular health in hemodialysis patients. The humble vitamin emerges as a potential vascular protector.
plos-pone-0343484: Indigenous Ethiopian zebu cattle endure heat that would fell imported breeds. This whole-genome sequencing study revealed divergent and shared selection signatures of heat stress adaptation in zebu from dry-hot and humid zones. The identified genes point the way toward climate-ready cattle for a warming world.
plos-pone-0357484: Digital financial literacy — comfort with fintech — shapes how households spend. This Chinese study examined its effect on household consumption, contrasting total expenditure against consumption structure. The findings link digital savvy to real spending patterns, with implications for financial inclusion policy.
plos-pone-0357384: Exercise sharpens adolescent minds — partly by quieting rumination, partly through mindfulness. This paper studied physical activity and executive function in adolescents, modeling dual rumination pathways with mindfulness as moderator. The model maps the mind-body link with unusual nuance.
plos-pone-0356184: Meningococcal disease didn’t pause for the pandemic. This paper laid out meningococcal disease epidemiology in the United States from 2020 to 2023. The surveillance data inform vaccination strategy in a period when many routine immunizations faltered.
plos-pone-0356884: A questionnaire measuring social determinants of health is only useful if it means the same thing everywhere. This paper tested the measurement and structural invariance of the social determinants of health questionnaire (SDH-Q) across countries. The validation enables genuine global comparisons of health’s social roots.
plos-pone-0354384: Nurse turnover bleeds hospitals dry — and predicting it could staunch the flow. This paper published a protocol for a systematic review of prediction models for nurse turnover. The planned review will separate the models that genuinely forecast departures from the ones that merely describe them.
plos-pone-0356684: Fiber-optic cables on coal shearers endure brutal heat underground. This paper characterized the temperature characteristics of fiber-optic shearer cables. The thermal data help engineers design cables that survive the mine’s inferno while carrying critical signals.
plos-pone-0355984: Autism’s biology remains elusive — but big data may crack it. This paper built an integrated systems biology and machine learning framework to identify potential biomarkers and pathways in autism spectrum disorder. The framework sifts genomic chaos for the signals that could one day enable early biological diagnosis.
plos-pone-0356784: Malnutrition wears two faces in Panama: undernutrition and obesity side by side. This paper documented the double burden among non-pregnant women of reproductive age using the country’s 2019 National Health Survey. The findings confront policymakers with a paradox — hunger and excess in the same population, sometimes the same household.
plos-pone-0356284: Studying retinal degeneration needs mouse models that mimic both slow and fast human disease. This paper generated dual mouse models with slow and rapid progression, driven by ectopic RIP3 expression. Having both tempos in one toolkit lets researchers test therapies against the full spectrum of degenerative speed. The models fill a critical gap in vision research.
plos-pone-0350484: How does a dolphin hear so exquisitely? This paper dissected the peripheral anatomy of the dolphin ear and its associated nervous structures using macroscopic dissection, DICE micro-CT, histology, and confocal microscopy. The multi-scale anatomical atlas reveals the biological engineering behind nature’s finest sonar — with lessons for human hearing science.
plos-pone-0354884: Women carrying BRCA1/2 mutations face agonizing family planning decisions. This subgroup analysis examined how decision coaching affects decisional conflict and decision status in healthy carriers with open family planning. The findings show structured coaching can genuinely ease one of medicine’s hardest choices.
plos-pone-0355784: The words we choose for family — kinship terms — are tangled up with grammar itself. This paper argued that word choice is coupled with grammar through the case of kinship. The linguistic analysis reveals that vocabulary and syntax aren’t separate modules but deeply interwoven systems.
plos-pone-0356384: A fungus living inside plants — Aspergillus fumigatus as an endophyte — can shield okra from salt and cadmium. This paper showed the endophyte modulates growth, oxidative stress, and cadmium accumulation under combined stresses. The fungal ally offers a biological route to farming contaminated, salty soils.
plos-pone-0335384: China’s Qinling mountains — a biodiversity treasure — need soil health monitoring. This paper assessed soil quality using TDS and MDS indicator methods. The comparative assessment establishes which measurement approach best captures the health of these ecologically vital mountain soils.
plos-pone-0326984: An old ankle sprain changes how you squat — in subtle, measurable ways. This paper compared kinematics and muscle activities during half squats in people with ankle sprain history versus controls. The altered movement patterns reveal compensations that persist long after the swelling fades — with implications for reinjury.
plos-pone-0353484: China’s hospital labs handle Streptococcus pneumoniae daily — but practices vary wildly. This national survey examined laboratory practices for specimen processing, pneumococcal identification, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing across CARSS hospitals. The findings expose the standardization gaps that undermine pneumonia surveillance — and patient care — nationwide.
plos-pone-0355284: CD93 — a cell surface protein — may drive stomach cancer’s growth and blood supply. This paper examined the effects of high CD93 expression on tumor growth and angiogenesis in gastric adenocarcinoma. The findings nominate CD93 as both a prognostic marker and a therapeutic target in a cancer that kills hundreds of thousands yearly.
plos-pone-0355684: Ethiopian women’s access to treatment for obstetric complications splits along the urban-rural divide. This multivariate decomposition analysis quantified those urban-rural disparities. The decomposed gaps tell policymakers exactly which factors — distance, wealth, education — drive the deadly divide.
plos-pone-0355484: Ireland needs nurse managers — but what makes nurses aspire to lead? This paper identified the key predictors of nurse management aspirations. The findings give health services a pipeline blueprint: understanding what draws nurses toward management is the first step to building the leadership the system needs.
plos-pone-0355384: Fragile X disorders go undiagnosed in Nigerian children — but public health screening could change that. The CHAMP-FX protocol outlines a prospective multicenter study to advance mental health through such screening. The planned research brings genetic diagnosis — and the interventions it unlocks — to children who’ve never had either.
europmc-pmc2813284: Do adult humans grow new brain cells like mice do? This 2010 paper compares neurogenesis in the human hippocampus with mice, across ages from birth to 100 years. The authors find human brains share the mouse pattern but at far lower levels, declining with age. The comparison grounded the debate about lifelong brain-cell growth in hard data.
europmc-pmc2819884: A rare but deadly fungal infection was rising in France, and this 2009 paper quantifies the trend. The authors track increasing cases of zygomycosis, also called mucormycosis, from 1997 to 2006. The surveillance data revealed a real and growing threat to vulnerable patients. The study pushed hospitals to watch for this difficult-to-treat infection.
europmc-pmc2858084: A stem-cell marker called ALDH1 may flag the toughest cells in tumors. This 2010 paper maps its levels and patterns across human epithelial cancers. The authors show where the marker runs high. Their atlas helps target the cells that reseed cancer after treatment.
europmc-pmc2916884: A few antibody flavors can neutralize many HIV strains. This 2010 paper shows a limited number of antibody specificities mediate broad and potent serum neutralization in select HIV-infected people. The authors' finding narrows the vaccine target. Their work focused the hunt.
europmc-pmc2918584: Chemists drowning in mass-spec data needed a life raft. This 2010 paper brings MZmine 2, a free toolkit for handling, viewing, and probing molecule readouts. The authors built it in snap-together parts. Their program became a bench staple in labs worldwide.
europmc-pmc2920084: Cycling is healthy but roads are risky. This 2010 paper asks whether the health benefits of cycling outweigh the risks. The authors weigh exercise gains against accidents and air pollution. Their math favors the bike by a wide margin. The study backed pro-cycling policy.
europmc-pmc2926784: A water mold rots crops worldwide, and this 2010 paper reads its genome. The authors sequence Pythium ultimum, revealing its attack tricks and its full set of effector weapons. Their genome exposes the enemy's toolkit. The data aids breeding crops that can resist it.
europmc-pmc2944084: Bisphenol A in pregnancy may seed blood sugar trouble for two generations. This 2010 mouse study finds BPA exposure during pregnancy disrupts glucose control in mothers and adult male offspring. The authors trace the metabolic fallout. Their work added diabetes to BPA's rap sheet.
europmc-pmc2946684: Gut bacteria that shrug off penicillin-like drugs threaten hospitals. This 2010 review covers extended-spectrum beta-lactamases, the enzymes behind the resistance. The authors survey where these enzymes strike. Their overview aids the antibiotic fight. Doctors lean on it when choosing last-resort drugs.
europmc-pmc3002984: Bugs beat bug-proof cotton through a pump mutation. This 2010 paper ties a cell-pump gene change to insect resistance against Bt toxin. The authors nail the resistance gene. Their work warns of spreading resistance. Refuge acres slow the resistance spread.
europmc-pmc3017084: Pooled DNA sequencing needs its own toolbox. This 2011 paper brings PoPoolation, software for studying gene pools from mixed samples. The authors' toolbox cut sequencing costs. It spread through labs. Fruit fly labs were early adopters. The tool handles millions of pooled reads.
europmc-pmc6533084: The stop-signal task - press a button, but halt when you hear the beep - is psychology's favorite measure of self-control. Dozens of labs run it slightly differently, muddying comparisons. This consensus guide from leading researchers standardizes how to run the task and score the ability to inhibit actions, so studies of impulsivity in ADHD, addiction, and beyond can finally speak the same language.
europmc-pmc6566984: People who eat more fiber tend to dodge heart disease - and the link is more than coincidence. This review explains how dietary fiber, the indigestible part of plants, lowers cholesterol, calms inflammation, and feeds good gut microbes. Against clogged arteries and heart attacks, the humble fiber emerges as a quiet protector.
europmc-pmc6617684: After a stroke, brain inflammation is both healer and destroyer. This review weighs neuroinflammation's double role in ischemic stroke: early immune responses that clear damage versus runaway inflammation that kills neurons. Understanding when inflammation helps or harms guides the timing of anti-inflammatory treatments.
europmc-pmc6631684: Both DNA and mRNA vaccines have simmered since the 1990s - but mRNA stole the spotlight. This review compares the two platforms head to head: the theory, the trial results, and the tradeoffs. Written before mRNA's pandemic triumph, it captures why the field bet on messenger RNA.
europmc-pmc6646484: Teaching computers to outline tumors and organs in scans - medical image segmentation - now leans on deep learning. This review surveys the wins and the sticking points: accuracy gains, data hunger, and trust issues. The field is strong but honest about what still blocks the clinic.
europmc-pmc6679484: Diagnosing Alzheimer's after death means reading the brain's scars: plaques, tangles, and vessel damage. This review lays out the neuropathological criteria pathologists use - what counts as Alzheimer's under the microscope and how the rules evolved. The definitive diagnosis still belongs to the autopsy suite.
europmc-pmc6709784: Plants fight disease with an arsenal of immune sensors - NLR genes that spot invading pathogens. This study catalogued the species-wide NLR inventory of Arabidopsis thaliana: every gene and its variants across the mustard weed's range. The full roster is a treasure map for breeding tougher crops.
europmc-pmc6717084: Blood pressure control is a tale of two worlds - even among rich nations. Comparing 12 high-income countries over time, this study tracked hypertension awareness, treatment, and control in adults aged 40 to 79. The trends reveal which health systems keep pressure down - and which let it slip.
europmc-pmc6744684: Collagen is the tumor's scaffolding - and it does more than hold things up. This review traces collagen's role in cancer from lab bench to bedside: how tumors remodel it, how it shapes their behavior, and how therapies might target it. The humble structural protein emerges as a player.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-84: A 2007 Government Accountability Office report assessing the United Nations' management reform efforts. Congress, which funds a large share of the UN budget, wanted to know whether promised reforms were working. GAO found progress had varied — some initiatives moved forward while others stalled. The report gives American lawmakers a scorecard on an institution they fund but do not control.
gao-gaoreports-b-309784: A Government Accountability Office bid-protest ruling dated October 19, 2007, covering two filings by CAMSS Shelters. The shelter manufacturer contested a federal contract award, and the consolidated decision works through each protest argument. The published ruling shows how GAO judges competitions for specialized equipment — and gives future bidders a map of what wins and what fails.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-584: Dangerous truckers were on GAO's radar in 2007 — the safety agency could name the risky carriers but would not say the maximum fines. The report finds the watchers spotting trouble yet pulling punches on penalties. The findings ask why the hammer stayed holstered when the bad actors were known.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-984: The Guard and Reserve's future had fine print in 2007 — GAO's report says money, security, and people puzzles should shape the force's redesign. The findings lay out the trade-offs. The report treats the citizen-soldier bargain as a contract worth reading closely.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-384: Veterans' college aid was a bureaucratic maze in 2007, and GAO's report says management action was needed to cut the overlap in approving programs. The findings target the duplication. The report argues the benefit should not require a second education to claim.
openalex-w7206159784: Medical school is famously grueling, long hours and early contact with suffering, and students pay a mental price. This study measures how common anxiety and depression are among medical students and what drives them. The authors frame the findings as a public-health concern inside the profession that treats everyone else's health. The paper adds hard numbers to a problem medical schools can no longer treat as background noise.
openalex-w7204997184: Dyslexia makes reading a daily struggle, and teachers need strategies, not just sympathy. This article examines how dyslexia affects teaching and learning, then lays out pedagogical approaches that help educators and schools support dyslexic students in the classroom. The authors focus on what actually works day to day. A practical guide that treats dyslexia as a teaching challenge with answers, not a verdict on a child's ability.
openalex-w7204176384: Bentham's panopticon was a prison of total watchfulness; today's workplace is its digital heir. This law article studies the new digital panopticon, constant monitoring of workers through software, and the challenges it poses to labor law. The authors trace the idea from Bentham through Foucault to the modern office. A sharp study of surveillance sold as productivity.
openalex-w7168300184: Batteries and electrolysis matter more every year, and this Japanese-language paper rethinks how we study them. The authors developed new analytical methods for electrode reactions that drop the old idealized assumptions. They aimed at real-world conditions like uneven pH. An electrochemistry methods paper for the energy age.
openalex-w7135014884: Curing hepatitis C is now possible, but metabolism can get in the way. This study tracked metabolic syndrome risk against adherence to direct-acting antiviral therapy over six months. The authors examined the two-way relationship. A hepatology study of treating the virus while the body complicates.
openalex-w7214972884: Zeolites are crystal sponges with molecule-sized holes, and tuning them tunes chemistry. This paper tells how iron was put back into zeolite beta and flaws were healed after the build. The team polished the active spots. A stuff-chemistry study of perfecting holey crystals.
pmc-13472284: A 2026 transplant paper tracking how patients fare after kidneys are assigned through out-of-sequence allocation under the newer KAS250 system. The study examines who receives these kidneys and how they do afterward, giving the transplant community early data on whether the system delivers organs fairly and effectively.
pmc-13439884: In this 2026 immunology paper, researchers found that IL-17-driven gene programs in muscle fibroblasts are not required for disease in a mouse model of Jo-1 myositis — an autoimmune muscle disease linked to anti-histidyl-tRNA synthetase antibodies. The negative result matters: it rules out a plausible mechanism and redirects the search. Careful falsification like this sharpens the path to real treatments.
pmc-13572084: This 2026 AI paper used dual-level knowledge distillation from a vision transformer to a Swin transformer for fine-grained brain tumor classification — a 44-class MRI benchmark. Distilling big models into efficient ones enables clinical deployment. The benchmark is the contribution.
pmc-13571484: In this 2026 antibody paper, researchers discovered a human antibody specific to the spike glycoprotein subunit 2 of SARS-CoV-2 and characterized its broad-spectrum neutralizing activity. S2 is more conserved than S1 across variants. The antibody is a pan-variant candidate.
pmc-13576384: This 2026 behavioral paper studied embodied morality in a disembodied world — dishonesty in real online interactions. The internet changes cheating. The real-interaction data are the strength.
pmc-13530684: A 2026 conference poster finding high satisfaction after leg fasciotomies for exertional compartment syndrome despite moderate symptom recurrence. Patients were happy even with some recurrence. The poster reports the paradox.
pmc-13530584: A 2026 conference poster finding combined MPFL reconstruction and tibial tubercle osteotomy did not decrease patellar height more than reconstruction alone. The combined surgery's effect was measured. The poster reports the equivalence.
pmc-13528284: A 2026 physical chemistry paper on nuclear motion's role in ultrafast relaxation of inner-shell vacancies in hydrated pyrrole. The X-ray-excited molecule's nuclei moved during electronic decay. The coupled dynamics are the finding.
pmc-13508584: A 2026 methods paper on estimands in Alzheimer's clinical trials — what treatment effects are being estimated and why it matters. The statistical clarity improves trials. The paper is the explainer.
pmc-13478784: A 2026 3-year follow-up of the Safe Early Intervention Approach's effects. The early childhood program's durability was tested. The follow-up is the evidence.
pmc-13478484: This 2026 paper used red cell distribution width and a modified 5-item frailty index to predict short-term mortality after hip fracture surgery. The simple markers forecasted death. The prediction aids surgical decisions.
pmc-13432784: A 2026 reproductive toxicology paper: industrial hydrocarbon exposure deteriorated sperm integrity and reproductive function. The petrochemicals harmed male fertility. The deterioration is the warning.
pmc-13431284: In this 2026 qualitative paper, care coordination experiences of whole families caring for children with medical complexity in rural areas were explored. The rural families' struggles were voiced. The experiences guide policy.
pmc-13456484: A 2026 chemistry paper on base-promoted benzylic C-H amination reactions across a wide pKa spectrum enabled by halobenzofuran and -indole oxidants. The amination's scope was broadened. The enabling is the synthetic advance.
pmc-13371584: A 2026 genome-wide association study of lean body mass response to resistance training in young Asians. The muscle-building genetics were mapped. The GWAS is the resource.
pmc-13309684: A 2026 veterinary paper establishing hematology and serum biochemistry reference intervals for captive-born owl monkeys — effects of age and sex. The primate normals were defined. The intervals serve research colonies.
pmc-13500784: In this 2026 natural products paper, context mattered — community and environmental context elicited natural products. The microbes produced more in context. The eliciting is the bioprospecting insight.
pmc-13459684: In this 2026 exploratory study, digital engagement and psychosocial health experiences were examined among late adolescents and young adults in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia (the title is truncated). The youth's digital lives were explored. The experiences inform policy.
pmc-13428184: In this 2026 paper, cytokine gene variants were associated with aerobic fitness-related, hematological, and metabolic traits in healthy adults. The immune genes' fitness link was found. The association is the genetic insight.
pmc-13476584: This 2026 enzymology paper showed trans-interface coupling in the tetrameric enzyme underlay allosteric control in E. coli biosynthetic threonine deaminase. The subunits communicated across interfaces. The coupling is the regulatory mechanism.
pmc-13473284: A 2026 Chinese study of boredom proneness and short-video addiction among vocational college students — psychological resilience as mediator, gender as moderator (the title is truncated). The boredom-addiction pathway was modeled. The mediating is the insight.
pmc-13426484: A 2026 review of research progress on multitarget mechanisms of terpenoids in ischemic stroke treatment. The plant compounds' stroke mechanisms were surveyed. The progress is the field's state.
pmc-13439284: A 2026 Swiss retrospective study of upfront unroofing of subepithelial lesions using cold snare in the upper and lower gastrointestinal tract. The endoscopic technique was evaluated. The unroofing is the approach.
arxiv-2606-16084: Sperm whales communicate in rhythmic click patterns called codas. This paper applies computational linguistics to test whether those codas show "duality of patterning" — the human-language property where meaningless sounds combine into meaningful units. The authors analyze the rhythm of the deep, asking how close whale communication comes to true language structure.
arxiv-2606-16284: Some theories predict new lightweight particles ("scalars") that decay invisibly — leaving no trace in a detector except missing energy. This paper studies how the proposed FCC-ee collider, a future electron-positron machine, could search for them. It targets particle physicists planning the physics program of next-generation colliders.
arxiv-2606-16584: A pure mathematics paper in several complex variables. It constructs the Perron–Bremermann envelope — a classical tool for solving boundary-value problems — for q-plurisubharmonic functions on unbounded domains in complex n-space. The work extends a standard technique to a rougher, more general setting for complex analysts.
arxiv-2606-16784: In quantum 'nonlocal games,' separated players use entanglement to win more often than classical players could. This paper studies such games played on graph ensembles — families of networks. It is a quantum information paper for researchers probing what entanglement makes possible.
arxiv-2606-16884: Tiny shake-beams can be pushed straight or pump-pushed (pumped at twice the beat). This paper tells the two pushes apart with a shaking carbon straw (nanotube). It is for tiny-shake pros. Two pushes, one tell. Tiny beams, clear answers. Shake it right.
